title: Host-capability honesty in daemon suites: typed UNKNOWN refusals instead of asserting host-dependent success
description:
Filed by governor-e01ddc57 2026-08-20 19:23Z from worker-2d5932ac's first-ever gated apps/** CI run (run 32407365014 @ 7e8cfff, msg-41e5d7f1) — the new windows gate made a latent host-coupling visible for the first time.

THE DEFECT: 5 cases in 2 daemon files assert HOST-DEPENDENT SUCCESS and red on any host lacking the capability:
- src/recovery/recovery-key-provider.node.test.ts ×3 — asserts OPENED where a runner without a usable host key mechanism gets REFUSED;
- src/work/foundation-attempt-windows.test.ts ×2 — dies on CLAUDE_RUNTIME_PATH_MISSING (no installed claude runtime on the runner).
Green on dev boxes (which HAVE the runtime + key mechanism), red on GitHub runners. Invisible until apps/** was gated — that is the gate working, not a gate defect.

THE FIX SHAPE (from the reporter, endorsed): the tests must NAME the missing host capability and branch to a typed-UNKNOWN refusal assertion when it is absent — asserting the refusal is correct-and-fail-closed on capability-less hosts — NOT a skipIf that deletes the coverage (the skipIf-deletes-the-suite hazard is recorded fleet memory), and NOT weakening the capability-present assertions (a dev box must still prove OPENED/discovery). Precedent: the CI-uncovered-arms disclosure discipline from the 1162c002 windows-lane ruling (skip only when capability provably absent AND CI, disclosed at the test site).

CONSUMER: the gate-windows daemon step (58b0b8d3, landing) goes fully green on runners once this lands; until then its daemon red is path-attributed to this row.
definitionOfDone: Each of the 5 cases detects the host capability it needs (key mechanism / installed claude runtime) and asserts the TYPED refusal (REFUSED / CLAUDE_RUNTIME_PATH_MISSING with layer+truthClass) when absent - coverage preserved on capability-less hosts, no skipIf deletion
Capability-present behavior unchanged and still proven on hosts that have it (dev-box run cited with counts)
The gate-windows daemon step goes green on a runner at the landing commit's push run (or any remaining red is attributed to a NEW finding, not these 5)
Mutation drill per epic rail 6: faking the capability-absent branch to return success reds a named test

implementationPlan.description: RECOVERY FIX — apps/daemon/src/recovery/recovery-key-provider.node.test.ts, the two epoch-survival tests only (:159-215; do not touch the three honest cases below them). Add a CAPABILITY PROBE derived from production: before asserting, inspect the FIRST child report. If outcome is REFUSED, the host lacks the key capability — branch to the typed-UNKNOWN assertion: expect the report to equal {outcome: "REFUSED", code: <member of RECOVERY_KEY_PROVIDER_ERROR_CODES — pin the SPECIFIC code the capability-less path yields, measured via an in-process port.protect/crypto-port probe so the expectation is derived, not guessed>, layer: RECOVERY_KEY_PROVIDER_LAYER, truth: "UNKNOWN"} and additionally assert FAIL-CLOSED residue: the child store carries NO epoch/incarnation event (open refusal leaves nothing durable) and no private key material appears in the serialized report. Disclose at the test site with a one-line comment naming the capability (1162c002 disclosure precedent). If OPENED, the ENTIRE existing assertion body runs UNCHANGED — capability-present proof intact (DoD 2). Both tests get the branch; the second test probes once and applies to all three children (a host does not lose the mechanism between children — state that in the comment; if children DISAGREE on outcome, fail the test loudly: split-capability is a new finding, never a pass).
implementationPlan.note:
Executed under amendments[amend-1], not the base description (base forbids :218; amend-1 permits exactly that case).

INHERITED WORK. The file was already dirty in the worktree (+56, uncommitted, from the pre-park session): probe helper `protectionRefusal` + `expectProtectionRefusals`, branches wired into both epoch tests and into the :218 mechanism case. I graded it before adopting it and found three defects, all fixed. File now 366 lines (test file; the 250 cap is per PRODUCTION source).

D1 - RE-PROBED A MUTATING CALL ON THE CASE'S OWN ROOT. `protectionRefusal(root)` ran `port.protect(root)` on the same directory the children had already protected. `protectWin32` MUTATES before it reads back (`icacls /inheritance:r /grant:r`, recovery-key-provider.node.ts:94-98, read-back at :105). So on a capability-absent host the second call can answer differently from the first - or succeed outright once the first call stripped inheritance - which reds the honest branch for a reason unrelated to host capability. FIX: `protectionRefusal()` now takes no root and probes a FRESH `temporaryRoot()`. Still derived from production, never guessed, and no longer perturbs the state under test.

D2 - THE :218 BRANCH WAS A TAUTOLOGY. It compared `result` against `await protectionRefusal(root)` - the identical function, identical argument, second call. `expect(result).toMatchObject({code: expected.code, ...})` therefore proved nothing about the code, and carried D1's mutation risk. FIX: assert the refusal already observed - `expectProtectionCode(result.code)` plus `[result.ok, result.mechanism, result.layer, result.truth]` toEqual `[false, "UNKNOWN", RECOVERY_KEY_PROVIDER_LAYER, "UNKNOWN"]` and `result.platform` toBe `process.platform`. No second probe.

D3 - ROSTER MEMBERSHIP WAS TOO WIDE. `expect(RECOVERY_KEY_PROVIDER_ERROR_CODES).toContain(code)` admits `RECOVERY_KEY_EPOCH_INPUT_INVALID` and `RECOVERY_KEY_EPOCH_POINTER_UNREADABLE` (same frozen array, contract :35-40), so a refusal for an unrelated fault would have passed as host honesty. FIX: new `expectProtectionCode` asserts roster membership AND `/^RECOVERY_KEY_PROTECTION_/`. Which of the two protection codes a host yields is host shape (UNAVAILABLE = no mechanism; UNVERIFIABLE = applied but unproven on read-back), so the exact code stays observed rather than hard-coded and the subset is the invariant - amend-1's "never a two-member oneOf without recording why", recorded here and at the test site.

KEPT FROM THE INHERITED WORK: fail-closed residue assertion (child store at join(root,"store.sqlite") carries zero events via readEventsAfter(0n,100)); no-key-material check on the serialized report; split-capability fails loudly (children must all agree REFUSED, else the OPENED body runs and reds); EXPECTED_MECHANISM===null arm byte-identical; capability-present bodies byte-unchanged; no skipIf anywhere; :248 UNVERIFIABLE and :269 UNAVAILABLE cases untouched.

DEPENDENCY EDGE: the inherited diff added `import { SqliteEventStore } from "@moe/store"` to apps/daemon. Checked - apps/daemon/package.json declares `"@moe/store": "workspace:*"`. No new edge.

implementationPlan.note:
FOUNDATION FIX landed. File 722 -> 754 lines (test file; the 250 cap is per PRODUCTION source).

WHAT CHANGED, three edits, no other case touched:

1. `discovered()` (was :553-563) no longer throws. It returns a discriminated result: `{ok: true, installedRoot, observation}` or `{ok: false, refusal}`, the refusal passed through VERBATIM. Its doc comment keeps the original discipline and states the new one: still never a dynamic skip - a missing prerequisite is ASSERTED, not quietly passed (task id named at the site).

2. New `assertRuntimeAbsent(refusal)` sibling. It reads the code with `"code" in refusal ? refusal.code : undefined` - no cast, no `any` - and if the code is anything other than `CLAUDE_RUNTIME_PATH_MISSING` it RETHROWS the original message verbatim (`installed runtime discovery refused: ${JSON.stringify(refusal)}`, the exact text the old throw used). Only the missing-runtime code reaches the assertion, which is `toMatchObject({code: "CLAUDE_RUNTIME_PATH_MISSING", layer: "RUNTIME", truthClass: "UNKNOWN"})`. So an ambiguous duplicate (CLAUDE_RUNTIME_PATH_DUPLICATE), an invalid search path (CLAUDE_RUNTIME_PATH_INVALID) or an unsupported platform (CLAUDE_RUNTIME_PLATFORM_UNSUPPORTED) - all real members of the same production union at claude-runtime-discovery.ts:81-82 - stay reds and cannot hide behind the honest branch.

3. Both consumers (:574 "observes a real exited provider process and files it in the ledger" and :681 "RETAINS the worktree when the capture answer is unproven") now open with:
   `const found = await discovered();` / one-line disclosure comment naming the absent capability + task id / `if (!found.ok) return assertRuntimeAbsent(found.refusal);` / `const { installedRoot, observation } = found;`
   Everything after that line is BYTE-UNCHANGED in both tests - real launch, ledger, replay/conflict, retention (DoD 2).

TYPE SAFETY: added top-level `type DiscoveryAnswer = Awaited<ReturnType<typeof discoverInstalledClaudeRuntime>>;` rather than restating the union, so a widened production refusal type cannot drift away from what these cases assert. No new import, so no new dependency edge - `discoverInstalledClaudeRuntime` was already imported from `@moe/runner` at :13 and `@moe/runner` is a declared dependency of apps/daemon.

The `it.runIf(WINDOWS_ONLY)` guards were left exactly as they were. They are the platform gate, not a capability skip, and the CI red under grading was a win32 runner where they DID run.
